materials.title: 5과 본문 — Pit Crews in Car Racing
materials.text:
You may only see the car and the driver during most car races, but there is a team behind the driver. This team is ⓐcalled a pit crew. A pit is a place on the side of the race track, and drivers stop there several times during a race. The main job of the pit crew is ⓑto check the car and change the tires. Changing the tires ⓒare especially important because the tires wear out ⓓeasily in a high speed race.
A pit stop can be as ⓔshort as 2 seconds, and there are as many as 20 members on a crew. Therefore, the pit crew has to work in perfect harmony. The driver may get all the attention, but as people say, "Races are won in the pits."

materials.title: 5과 본문 — Pacers in a Marathon
materials.text:
Pacers run with other runners and lead them in a marathon. Pacers are experienced runners, and their job is to help other runners manage their race better. There can be several pacers in a race.
Each pacer runs at different speeds and finishes the race in different times. Pacers usually have flags or balloons showing their finish time.
Runners can choose a pacer depending on their target finish time. For example, if a runner wants to finish the race in four hours, the runner will follow the four-hour pacer. Since the pacer keeps track of the time, the runner can achieve his or her goal of finishing the marathon in a particular time more easily. In short, ______________________.

materials.title: 5과 대화 — Sports World
materials.text:
W: Hello. Welcome to Sports World. May I help you?
B: Yes, I came to register for a swimming class.
W: Is this your first time taking swimming lessons?
B: Yes, it is. I don't know how to swim at all.
W: I see. How often do you want to take classes?
B: I want to take classes twice a week. I'd like to take classes on weekdays and not on weekends.
W: Then, I suggest that you take the Beginner 2 class. This class meets on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
B: That sounds good. I'd like to sign up for that class. How big is the class?
W: The class has a limit of 10 people.
B: That's perfect.

materials.title: 〈보기〉
materials.text:
(a) A pit stop can be as short as 2 seconds.
(b) There are as much as 20 members on a crew.
(c) Sherpas are as important as the climbers.
(d) This rope is three times as longer as that one.
(e) Pacers don't run as fast as they can.
(f) My bag is twice as heavy as yours.
(g) The tires wear out as easy as paper.

materials.title: 6과 본문 — One Lucky Sunday (1)
materials.text:
Cyril Boggis was an antique furniture dealer in London. He was known for buying good things at a low price and then selling them at a high price. ( ① ) People asked him where he had got the furniture, but he just said, "It's a secret." ( ② )
Mr. Boggis' secret was simple. He went to small towns every Sunday and knocked on doors. ( ③ ) He told people that he was a furniture dealer. ( ④ ) He was able to buy things very cheaply. ( ⑤ )
Now it was another Sunday, and Mr. Boggis was in a small town again.

materials.title: 〈보기〉
materials.text:
(a) When Mr. Boggis came back, the legs had been cut off.
(b) People asked him where he has got the furniture.
(c) Bert had already cut off the legs before Mr. Boggis returned.
(d) I had lost my smartphone, so I looked for it at the snack shop.
(e) He realized that he had leave his wallet at home.

materials.title: 6과 본문 — One Lucky Sunday (2)
materials.text:
"How much?" Rummins asked.
"Not much, I'm afraid. This is just a reproduction," said Mr. Boggis.
"So how much?"
"Ten pounds."
"Ten? It's worth more than that."
"How about fifteen?"
"Make it fifty."
"Well, thirty. This is my final offer."
"OK, it's yours, but how are you going to take it? This thing will not go in a car!"
"We'll see," Mr. Boggis said and went out to bring his car.

materials.title: 6과 본문 — One Lucky Sunday (3)
materials.text:
On his way to the car, Mr. Boggis couldn't help ⓐsmiling. The table was what every dealer dreamed of. He couldn't believe his ⓑluck.
"Dad, what if this thing doesn't go in his car? He might not pay you," said Bert.
Rummins then had an idea. "What he wants is only the ⓒlegs. Let's cut the legs off for him," said Rummins. "Great idea!" said Bert. Bert then took out a saw and began to cut off the legs.
When Mr. Boggis came back, the legs had been cut off. "Don't worry, this was a favor. I won't ⓓcharge you for this," said Rummins. Mr. Boggis was so ⓔpleased that he couldn't say anything.

materials.title: 6과 대화 — Romeo and Juliet
materials.text:
B: Excuse me, Ms. Carter. Can I ask you a question? Did I get the main role in the play?
W: Yes, you did. Congratulations, Jiho! You're going to be Romeo in our school play, Romeo and Juliet.
B: Really? I'm so excited. Thank you so much, Ms. Carter.
W: I know how much you wanted the role. ______________________
B: Thank you. What about Sumi? Did she get the role she wanted, too?
W: Unfortunately, no. She's very disappointed.
B: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Anyway, when is the first practice?
W: It's at 2 p.m. on September 20th, in the acting club room.

materials.title: 7과 본문 — Living with Big Data
materials.text:
Have you ever visited an online bookstore and ⓐbeen surprised by the books that the store recommended for you? Many of them looked ⓑinteresting to you. So how did the bookstore know what you liked? This is all possible because of big data.
What is big data?
Big data is data sets that are very big and complex. As information and communication technology develops, the amount of data we have is getting ⓒmuch greater than before. This is mainly because almost everything that we do online ⓓleave a trace. For example, the photos you upload on your blog and the records of your purchases at online stores are all part of big data.
Simply collecting data, however, is not enough. Big data has to be analyzed, and this is done by big data experts. ⓔUsing various methods, experts analyze big data and draw meaningful results from it. These results then can be used to make decisions or to predict the future.

materials.title: 7과 본문 — Improving Performance in Sports
materials.text: Are you a sports fan? Well, big data is improving the performance of players, making sports more exciting. A famous example is Germany's national soccer team. The team built a database by collecting and analyzing a huge amount of data on players. For example, the data included information about how much each player ran and how long he had the ball. With the help of this database, Germany's national soccer team was able to improve its performance and win the 2014 World Cup.

materials.title: 외부지문 — Fly Away Home (1)
materials.text:
My dad and I live in an airport. That's because we don't have a home and the airport is better than the streets. We are careful not to get caught. Mr. Slocum and Mr. Vail were caught last night. "Ten green bottles, hanging on the wall," they sang. They were as loud as two moose bellowing. Dad says they broke the first rule of living here. Don't get noticed.
Dad and I try not to get noticed. We stay among the crowds. We change airlines. "Delta, TWA, Northwest, we love them all," Dad says. He and I wear blue jeans and blue T-shirts and blue jackets. We each have a blue zippered bag with a change of blue clothes. Not to be noticed is to look like nobody at all.

materials.title: 외부지문 — Fly Away Home (7) · (8)
materials.text:
(7) When Dad comes home from work, he buys hamburgers for us and the Medinas. That's to pay them for watching out for me. If Denny and I've had a good day, we treat for pie. But I've stopped doing that. I save my money in my shoe. "Will we ever have our own apartment again?" I ask Dad. I'd like it to be the way it was, before Mom died. "Maybe we will," he says. "If I can find more work. If we can save some money."
(8) But I know he's trying all the time to find us a place. He takes newspapers from the trash baskets and makes pencil circles around letters and numbers. Then he goes to the phones. When he comes back he looks sad. Sad and angry. I know he's been calling about an apartment. I know the rents are too high for us. "I'm saving money, too," I tell him, and I lift one foot and point to my shoe. Dad smiles. "Atta boy!"

materials.title: 외부지문 — Helping Each Other Makes Society Stronger
materials.text:
In every community, people rely on one another in both small and big ways. Working together and helping others is not only kind but also essential for a healthy society. When neighbors share their time, skills, or resources, they make life easier and safer for everyone.
For example, after a big storm, some people clear fallen trees from the streets, while others deliver food and blankets to families who cannot leave their homes. In schools, students help classmates who are struggling with homework or share books and supplies. In hospitals, volunteers assist nurses and doctors by bringing water, guiding visitors, and comforting patients. Even children can help by picking up trash in parks or planting trees in their neighborhoods. Every action, no matter how small, matters.

materials.text:
(a) The man sitting next to Mina is her uncle.
(b) What I need now are a cup of hot tea.
(c) Changing tires quickly is as important as driving fast.

items.stem_ko: 다음 중 단어와 영영풀이의 연결이 바르지 않은 것은?
options: register – to put your name on an official list
trace – a mark or sign showing that someone or something was there
harmony – a state of working well together without disagreement
purchase – something that you have bought
items.why_ko: hire 는 「(돈을 주고) 사람을 쓰다 · 고용하다」 (to pay someone to work for you). 「고용을 그만두다」 는 fire.

items.stem_ko: 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것은?
items.why_ko: 동명사구 주어(Changing the tires)는 단수 → is. ⓐ 「팀이 ~라고 불린다」 수동태 ⓑ 보어 자리 to부정사 ⓓ 동사 wear out 을 꾸미는 부사 ⓔ as + 원급(형용사) + as.

items.stem_ko: 윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
options: How much money does a pit crew member earn?
What is the main job of a pit crew?
Why is changing the tires especially important?
How many members can there be on a crew?
items.why_ko: 피트 크루의 보수는 나오지 않는다. ② 경주로 옆 ③ 차 점검 · 타이어 교체 ④ 고속 경주에서 타이어가 쉽게 닳아서 ⑤ 20명까지.

items.stem_ko: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
options: pacers run hard to win the race themselves
pacers run not to win but to help others
every runner has to finish in four hours
pacers run only when they are paid well
the fastest runner always becomes a pacer
items.why_ko: 페이서는 다른 주자가 목표 시간에 완주하도록 돕는다 → 이기려고가 아니라 남을 위해 달린다 (본문: pacers run but they don't run to win. They run for others.)

items.stem_ko: 위 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
options: 소년은 수영을 전혀 할 줄 모른다.
Beginner 2 반은 화요일과 목요일에 수업이 있다.
소년은 주말에 수업을 듣고 싶어 한다.
items.why_ko: on weekdays and not on weekends — 주말이 아니라 주중에 듣고 싶어 한다.

items.stem_ko: 〈보기〉에서 어법상 옳은 문장의 개수는?
items.why_ko: 옳은 것 (a)(c)(e)(f) 4개. (b) 셀 수 있는 members → as many as (d) 배수사 + as + 원급 → as long as (g) 동사 wear out 을 꾸미므로 부사 → as easily as.

items.stem_ko:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 다음 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
「People didn't know how valuable their things were, so Mr. Boggis took advantage of them.」
items.why_ko: 가구상이라고 밝힘 → 사람들은 물건 값어치를 몰랐고 Boggis 가 그것을 이용함 → 그래서 아주 싸게 살 수 있었다. ⑤ 에 넣으면 「싸게 샀다」 뒤에 이유가 오고, 다음 단락(또 다른 일요일)과 끊긴다.

items.stem_ko: 〈보기〉에서 어법상 옳은 문장만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
items.why_ko: (b) 묻던 때(과거)보다 앞선 일 → had got (e) had + 과거분사 → had left. (a) 다리가 잘린 것이 돌아온 것보다 먼저 · 수동 (c)(d) 앞선 일을 had p.p. 로.

items.stem_ko: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
options: Mr. Boggis first offered fifteen pounds.
Mr. Boggis finally agreed to pay fifty pounds.
Rummins thought the table would easily go in the car.
Mr. Boggis carried the table to his car by himself.
items.why_ko: "Make it fifty." — Rummins 가 50파운드를 불렀다. ① 처음 제안은 10 ③ 최종 30 ④ 차에 안 들어간다고 함 ⑤ 차를 가지러 나갔다.

items.stem_ko: 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.why_ko: 값진 18세기 탁자의 다리가 잘려 나갔으니 너무 놀라(shocked) 말을 못 한 것. pleased(기쁜)는 반대. ⓐ 웃지 않을 수 없었다 ⓑ 운 ⓒ 다리(Boggis 가 다리만 쓰겠다고 했다) ⓓ (돈을) 청구하다.

items.stem_ko: 윗글의 밑줄 친 this was a favor 에서 Rummins 가 말한 「호의」의 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
options: 탁자 다리를 미리 잘라 준 것
부러진 탁자 다리를 고쳐 준 것
items.why_ko: Boggis 가 다리만 필요하다고 했으니, 차에 실을 수 있게 다리를 잘라 준 것을 호의라고 했다 (아이러니).

items.stem_ko: 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
options: I hope you feel better soon.
items.why_ko: 주인공 역을 따 기뻐하는 지호에게 함께 기뻐해 주는 말 → B 가 Thank you 로 받는다. 나머지는 유감 · 위로.

items.stem_ko:
다음 두 문장을 한 문장으로 바르게 연결한 것은?
「Bert cut off the legs. Then Mr. Boggis came back with his car.」
options: When Mr. Boggis came back with his car, Bert has cut off the legs.
When Mr. Boggis had come back with his car, Bert cut off the legs.
When Mr. Boggis came back with his car, Bert had been cut off the legs.
When Mr. Boggis came back with his car, Bert had cut off the legs.
When Mr. Boggis comes back with his car, Bert had cut off the legs.
items.why_ko: 먼저 일어난 일(다리를 자름)을 had p.p., 나중 일(돌아옴)을 과거로. ② 순서가 뒤바뀜 ③ Bert 가 직접 잘랐으니 능동 ① 현재완료는 과거 시점과 못 씀 ⑤ 시제 불일치.

items.stem_ko: 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것은?
items.why_ko: 주어 almost everything (that we do online) 은 단수 → leaves. ⓐ Have you ever ~ and been p.p. (현재완료 병렬) ⓑ look + 형용사 보어 ⓒ 비교급 강조 much ⓔ 분사구문(= As they use ~).

items.stem_ko:
윗글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
「Big data comes from the (A)______ we leave online, but it becomes useful only after experts (B)______ it.」
items.why_ko: 온라인에서 하는 거의 모든 일이 흔적(trace)을 남겨 빅데이터가 되고, 모으기만 해서는 안 되고 분석(analyze)해야 쓸모가 있다. ④ collect 는 「Simply collecting data is not enough」 와 반대.

items.stem_ko: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
options: 독일 팀은 데이터베이스 덕분에 2018년 월드컵에서 우승했다.
독일 국가대표 축구팀은 선수들에 관한 데이터베이스를 만들었다.
데이터에는 각 선수가 얼마나 많이 뛰었는지가 들어 있었다.
데이터에는 각 선수가 공을 얼마나 오래 가졌는지가 들어 있었다.
items.why_ko: 독일 팀이 우승한 것은 2014년 월드컵이다.

items.stem_ko: 다음 중 분사구문을 부사절로 바꾼 것이 바르지 않은 것은?
options:
Having no home, Andrew and his dad live in an airport.
→ Although they have no home, Andrew and his dad live in an airport.

Using various methods, experts analyze big data.
→ As they use various methods, experts analyze big data.

Turning left, you will find the library.
→ If you turn left, you will find the library.

Feeling tired, I went to bed early.
→ Because I felt tired, I went to bed early.

Walking along the street, I met my teacher.
→ While I was walking along the street, I met my teacher.
items.why_ko: 집이 없어서 공항에 산다 → 이유(Because/As). Although(양보)는 뜻이 반대가 된다.

items.stem_ko: 윗글의 밑줄 친 broke the first rule of living here 의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
options: 남의 눈에 띄지 말라는 규칙을 어겼다
items.why_ko: 바로 뒤 「Don't get noticed.」 가 첫째 규칙 — 두 사람은 큰 소리로 노래해 눈에 띄었다가 잡혔다.
underline: Dad says they [broke the first rule of living here]

items.stem_ko: 윗글에 드러난 'I'(Andrew)의 바람으로 가장 적절한 것은?
options: 메디나 가족과 파이를 자주 사 먹는 것
엄마가 계시던 때처럼 우리 집에서 사는 것
아빠와 함께 신문을 모으는 일을 하는 것
모은 돈으로 새 신발을 사는 것
items.why_ko: "Will we ever have our own apartment again?" · I'd like it to be the way it was, before Mom died. 파이 사 먹기는 그만두고 신발에 돈을 모은다.

items.stem_ko: 윗글에서 서로 돕는 예로 언급되지 않은 것은?
options: 폭풍이 지난 뒤 쓰러진 나무 치우기
집을 나설 수 없는 가정에 음식 전달하기
items.why_ko: 스마트폰 사용법 가르치기는 나오지 않는다. ①② 폭풍 뒤 ④ 학교 ⑤ 병원 자원봉사.

items.stem_ko: 〈보기〉에서 어법상 옳은 문장만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
items.why_ko: (a) 명사를 뒤에서 꾸미는 현재분사 (c) 동명사 주어 단수 · as + 원급 + as (d) 수동 분사구문(= As they were born). (b) What 절 주어는 단수 → is (e) 말한 때보다 앞선 일 → had cut (f) how to use.

essays.prompt_ko: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작할 때, 1번째·2번째·6번째 단어를 쓰시오.
essays.context: 어디서 범죄가 일어날지 알지 못해서, 경찰은 그것을 막을 수 없었다.
conditions: 분사구문으로 시작할 것 (접속사를 쓰지 말 것)
주어진 단어를 모두 사용하되 필요하면 형태를 바꿀 것
「경찰」 은 the police 로, could not 은 couldn't 로 줄여 쓸 것
답안에는 지정된 순서의 단어만 쓸 것
essays.why_ko: Not knowing where crime would happen, the police couldn't prevent it. — 분사구문의 부정은 not 을 분사 앞에. 간접의문문 where + 주어 + 동사 (would/will 뒤 동사원형 happen).

essays.prompt_ko: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작할 때, 4번째·7번째 단어를 쓰시오.
essays.context: 완주 시간을 보여 주는 깃발을 들고 있는 페이서를 따라가라.
conditions: 관계대명사를 쓰지 말고 분사를 사용할 것
주어진 단어를 모두 사용하되 필요하면 형태를 바꿀 것
명령문으로 쓰고, 깃발은 a flag, 페이서 · 완주 시간 앞에는 the 를 쓸 것
답안에는 지정된 순서의 단어만 쓸 것
essays.why_ko: Follow the pacer holding a flag showing the finish time. — 「~하고 있는」 은 명사 뒤 현재분사.

essays.prompt_ko: 다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 부분 2곳을 찾아 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
essays.context:
Mr. Boggis went out to bring his car. On his way to the car, he couldn't help to smile.
Meanwhile, Bert took out a saw and began to cut off the legs.
When Mr. Boggis came back, the legs had cut off.
conditions: 한 칸에 「틀린 말 → 고친 말」 로 쓸 것
essays.answer_en:
